value.rationale: The mathematical gap is whether the familiar single-retention-unit storm-order single-crossing behavior survives aggregation of realistic heterogeneous roof types. An exact two-type counterexample exhibits three alternations with the same common rainfall pair and same initial fractional wetness; a proof that one roof cannot do this establishes sharp minimum structural complexity. This is a motivated aggregation limitation useful as a benchmark and model-diagnostic caution, not an arbitrary parameter-only recomputation. Exact roots matter because they rule out grid artifacts and delimit all sign intervals. No empirical universal or calibrated policy claim is made.
